newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish debt succumbed to bears on Monday, ending with losses as other European markets were adding downward pressure amid fresh worries over EMU.

Speculation grew that French President Jacques Chirac would announce later today a snap election, seen as necessary to allow the government to push through measures for France to qualify for Europe's single currency start.

"It's not only France, it's that now the market thinks an EMU delay is more likely. France's outlook of course is adding pressure," a dealer in Madrid said. The peseta also lost ground versus the mark in line with other crosses, dealers said.
Despite a gloomy technical outlook, dealers said it was difficult to make forecasts on the market trend short term.
"Nothing clear is happening here. I just see sideways trade...we're just tracking others," a dealer in Madrid said.
Technical analysts said the long future could dip toward 112 without any mayor resistance.
At midday bonos were supported by a positive trend in the Italian market discounting benign provisional April CPI.
